title: I guess you could say it was a GIANT let down 😅 #Broadway #BroadwayPl...
transcript: Giant starring John Lithgow could have been a really good play, but instead I left the theatre feeling like this could have been an email. This play is a character study of Roald Dahl, played by Lithgow, and explores the anti Semitic sentiments that he developed later in life. And this play can be a tough watch at times, as you're basically just watching a man double down on his anti Semitism for two hours straight. And while I think Lithgow's performance is great, I don't really feel as though the play itself had very much to say. There are certainly some thought provoking ideas in here. There is literally one two minute scene that touches on the art versus artist debate. I thought it did a decent job highlighting how, when confronted with biases, people have a tendency to get really defensive and double down rather than actually listen to the criticism. The problem is, rather than explore these interesting and novel ideas that it kind of teases throughout, the play instead chooses to dedicate a majority of its run time to rehashing the Israel Palestine debate that we have seen play out ad nauseam over the past couple years. And that's not necessarily its fault. It was written prior to the events of October 7th, and I do have to wonder if it premiered 3, 4 years ago, if I would feel differently. But when viewed in 2026, it doesn't really feel like it's bringing anything new to The conversation. And while in general I didn't find this play to be overly preachy, it is impossible to ignore that the person that they chose to represent the anti Israel side of this debate also happens to be a raging anti Semite. And so a lot of the nuance kind of goes out the window. And I just left the theatre wondering what we as an audience were supposed to take from this. If the goal was to write an Israel Palestine debate play, I don't think Roald Dahl was the best conduit. And if your goal was to write a Roald Dahl character study, then why are you spending 80% of your run time talking about Israel/ Palestine? It just feels like it's trying to have its cake and eat it too, and in the process it's not really achieving either goal. Like, it's wild to me that art versus the artist only takes up two minutes of this plays run time.
classificationReason: Creator attended and left the theatre with a clear negative opinion ('could have been an email'). Critiques the play's lack of depth, praises Lithgow's performance, and analyzes specific thematic choices — a first-hand review of the live production.
